note — the bold part is what the card te: Many der-words add -e. In the plural the article is always die, whatever the gender.
der Tisch → Tische: -e, no umlaut.
der Tag → Tage.
das Jahr → Jahre. Jahre alt is the full way to give an age.
Some words add -e and an umlaut: Stuhl → Stühle.
der Zug → Züge: u becomes ü.
die Stadt → Städte: a becomes ä, plus -e.
der Baum → Bäume: au becomes äu.
Many das-words add -er: Kind → Kinder. The verb is plural: spielen.
-er comes with an umlaut where it can: Buch → Bücher.
das Haus → Häuser: umlaut plus -er.
das Land → Länder. viele: many, with a plural.
das Bild → Bilder: -er, no umlaut possible.
das Ei → Eier.
das Glas → Gläser: a becomes ä, plus -er.
Most die-words add -n or -en: Frau → Frauen.
A word in -e adds only -n: Katze → Katzen.
die Frage → Fragen.
ein has no plural: a flower, but just flowers — Blumen with no article.
die Flasche → Flaschen. German needs no word for of here.
die Tomate → Tomaten.
A die-word in -el adds -n: Kartoffeln.
Words in -ung always add -en: Zeitungen.
-in doubles its n before -en: Freundinnen.
Words ending in a vowel other than -e, often from other languages, add -s: Autos.
das Handy, the German word for a mobile, takes -s: Handys.
das Foto → Fotos.
der-words in -er add nothing: der Lehrer, die Lehrer. Only the article shows the plural.
das Zimmer → die Zimmer: no ending.
Words in -en add nothing: Kuchen.
-chen words never change: das Mädchen, die Mädchen. das, because -chen makes every word neuter.
Some der-words in -er only add an umlaut: Bruder → Brüder.
der Apfel → Äpfel: umlaut only.
die Tochter → Töchter: umlaut only. ihre, as ein would have in the plural.
der Junge → Jungen: masculine words in -e add -n.
die Eltern only exists in the plural; the possessive takes -e: meine.
Geschwister: brothers and sisters together, a plural with no ending.
kein has a plural: keine Kinder, while ein has none.
